title: The side of an attack
hook: Follow a nucleophile as a leaving group departs.

knows: A nucleophile can donate an electron pair to form a bond.
doesNotKnow: In an SN2 reaction, backside attack and departure occur in one step, with inversion at the reacting carbon.

misconception: The nucleophile enters from the same side as the departing group.
objective: Recognize backside attack, simultaneous bond changes and inversion in an SN2 reaction.

claims.text: Question, diagram, and explanation: In an SN2 substitution, from which side does the nucleophile approach the carbon bearing the leaving group? In an SN2 reaction, backside attack and departure occur in one step, with inversion at the reacting carbon.

Recall: In an SN2 reaction, what happens at the carbon as the nucleophile replaces the leaving group? In an SN2 reaction, backside attack and departure occur in one step, with inversion at the reacting carbon.
The transition state is not a stable intermediate; the old and new bonds are partial in the transition state.

recall.question: In an SN2 reaction, what happens at the carbon as the nucleophile replaces the leaving group?
options: Its arrangement always stays the same
It forms a stable carbocation first
recall.why: In an SN2 reaction, backside attack and departure occur in one step, with inversion at the reacting carbon.
